name: The twelve spines
note: One hundred and seventy-five regional events. Every spine now runs from its region's own beginning to 1947 or close to it, with no century in which a player's own region has nothing to say. Kashmir stopped at 1400 and Sri Lanka at 1160; both now reach the twentieth century.

events.title: Burzahom's second phase: houses come above ground
events.evidence: The stratigraphy at Burzahom, where the pit dwellings are succeeded by mud-brick structures on the old floors.

events.title: Wheat, barley and lentils are grown in the valley
events.evidence: Carbonised grain from Burzahom and Gufkral, with the earliest Kashmir dates for domesticated cereals.

events.title: The dog burials at Burzahom: an animal interred with its owner
events.evidence: The excavated graves, in which dogs and in one case an antler were placed with the human remains.
events.note: A practice with no parallel elsewhere in the Indian Neolithic. Kashmir was looking north.

events.title: The harvester knife arrives from the Chinese Neolithic
events.evidence: The rectangular perforated harvesting knives at Burzahom, whose closest parallels are in north China.

events.title: Menhirs are raised at Burzahom
events.evidence: The standing stones at the site, set up over the earlier occupation.

events.title: Semthan: the valley's iron-age and early historic sequence
events.evidence: The excavated sequence at Semthan, which carries Kashmir from megalithic levels into the Indo-Greek period.

events.title: Indo-Greek and Kushan coins circulate in the valley
events.evidence: Coin finds at Semthan, Ushkur and Harwan, and the Kushan-period terracotta tiles.

events.title: Harwan's tiled monastery courtyard
events.evidence: The moulded and numbered terracotta tiles, laid in sequence — the numbering is a builder's instruction.

events.title: Naga cults and the valley's spring shrines are absorbed into Shaivism
events.evidence: The Nilamata Purana, which is a ritual gazetteer of the valley's springs, and the shrine sites themselves.

events.title: The Nilamata Purana describes the valley as a drained lake
events.evidence: The text, whose festival calendar and site list Kalhana used five centuries later as a source.

events.title: The Karkotas take the valley and hold the passes
events.evidence: Kalhana's chronology, and the Karkota coin series.

events.title: Kashmiri monks translate for the Tang court
events.evidence: The Chinese Buddhist catalogues, which name Kashmiri translators and their works.

events.title: Suyya re-engineers the Jhelum and moves a town to do it
events.evidence: Kalhana's detailed account of the dredging, the stone embankments, and the resulting fall in grain prices.
events.note: A chronicle that records what happened to the price of rice afterwards. That is an economic source.

events.title: Anandavardhana argues that poetry means by suggestion
events.evidence: The Dhvanyaloka, and the commentarial tradition that runs from it to Abhinavagupta.

events.title: Kshemendra writes satires on the professions of his own city
events.evidence: The Narmamala and Desopadesa, which name the clerk, the physician and the bawd and describe their frauds.

events.title: The Lohara dynasty, and Didda rules in her own name
events.evidence: Kalhana's account, and the Lohara coin series.

events.title: Famine and flood in the valley, recorded year by year
events.evidence: Kalhana's chronicle, which gives the grain price and the mortality for successive years.

events.title: The Shah Mir sultanate takes the valley
events.evidence: The Persian chronicles of Kashmir and the sultanate's coinage.
events.becomes: A Persianate court in the valley, the Kashmiri shawl industry organised under state patronage, and the papier-mache and carpet trades that came with craftsmen brought from Samarkand.

events.title: The Rishi order: Nund Rishi and a Kashmiri Sufism with local roots
events.evidence: The shruks of Nund Rishi, and the shrine network of the order.
events.note: It grew out of Lal Ded's verse as much as out of Persian Sufism. The valley made its own.

events.title: Temple destruction under Sikandar, and the argument about its scale
events.evidence: The Persian chronicles, which claim it; the surviving temples, which complicate it; and Jonaraja's continuation of the Rajatarangini.

events.title: Zain-ul-Abidin reverses the policy and has the Sanskrit texts recopied
events.evidence: Jonaraja and Srivara's chronicles, and the translation projects into Persian he commissioned.
events.note: Called Budshah, the great king, four hundred years later and still. He rebuilt what his father's reign had burned.

events.title: The Kashmir shawl becomes a global luxury export
events.evidence: The workshop records, the European inventories, and the French and Scottish imitations that followed.

events.title: The Mughals annex the valley and build gardens in it
events.evidence: The Akbarnama, and the Shalimar and Nishat garden records.

events.title: The Treaty of Amritsar sells the valley to the Dogras
events.evidence: The treaty itself, which names the sum, and the Company's correspondence about it.
events.note: A territory transferred by sale between two other parties. The game should let the player feel what that means.

events.title: The 1885 Kashmir earthquake
events.evidence: The contemporary survey reports and the damage assessments from Srinagar and Baramulla.

events.title: Stein edits the Rajatarangini and walks the valley to check it
events.evidence: His edition and translation, and the topographical memoir in which he identified Kalhana's place names on the ground.
events.note: He checked a twelfth-century chronicle by walking to every place it named. Most of them were there.

events.title: Balangoda: forty thousand years of occupation before any of this
events.evidence: The Fa Hien and Batadombalena cave sequences, with the earliest anatomically modern human remains in South Asia.
events.note: The island's record is older than the campaign. The game opens partway through somebody's story.

events.title: Cereal pollen and burning at Horton Plains
events.evidence: The Horton Plains pollen core, which shows forest clearance and cereal-type pollen far earlier than expected.

events.title: Iron and Brahmi at Anuradhapura, on potsherds
events.evidence: The Anuradhapura citadel excavation, with radiocarbon-dated Brahmi-inscribed sherds from the earliest levels.

events.title: Cave drip-ledge inscriptions: the island's oldest writing, and it names donors
events.evidence: Some twelve hundred inscribed drip-ledges, recording gifts of caves to the sangha by named householders.

events.title: The great tanks and the bisokotuwa sluice
events.evidence: The surviving sluice structures, whose valve-pit design regulates outflow pressure — the earliest known solution to the problem.
events.note: A valve tower that lets water out at a controlled pressure. Nobody else built one for a thousand years.

events.title: The Dipavamsa: the island writes its own history
events.evidence: The text, the earliest surviving Sri Lankan chronicle, and its relationship to the Mahavamsa that follows.

events.title: The Mahavamsa, and a chronicle tradition kept continuously for sixteen centuries
events.evidence: The text and its continuations, maintained without a break into the modern period.
events.note: The longest unbroken historical record in South Asia, and it is kept by monks, not by a state.

events.title: Sigiriya is abandoned and returned to the sangha
events.evidence: The site's occupation sequence, the graffiti on the mirror wall, and the Culavamsa's account.

events.title: The Sigiriya mirror wall graffiti: seven centuries of visitors' verse
events.evidence: Some seven hundred legible verses scratched by visitors between the sixth and thirteenth centuries, many by women.
events.note: Tourists writing poetry on a wall, dated by their own handwriting. An accidental corpus.

events.title: The three nikayas are unified under the Mahavihara
events.evidence: Parakramabahu's Galvihara inscription, which sets out the terms of the reform.

events.title: Magha of Kalinga takes Polonnaruwa and the dry zone is abandoned
events.evidence: The Culavamsa's account, and the archaeological evidence for the abandonment of the tank civilisation.
events.note: The tanks silt up and the population moves southwest. A thousand years of hydraulic engineering ends in a generation.

events.title: The capital moves southwest, and keeps moving
events.evidence: The Dambadeniya, Yapahuwa, Kurunegala and Gampola sequence in the Culavamsa and the building record.

events.title: Cinnamon becomes the island's export and then its problem
events.evidence: The Arab and Chinese trade records, and the Portuguese monopoly that followed.

events.title: Kotte, Jaffna and Kandy: three kingdoms on one island
events.evidence: The Sinhala and Tamil chronicle traditions and the Portuguese accounts of all three.

events.title: The Portuguese take the coast and cannot take the highlands
events.evidence: The Portuguese records, and the Kandyan accounts of the campaigns that failed.
events.becomes: A Catholic coastal population, a Portuguese-derived creole, and a Kandyan kingdom that survives by being unreachable — for another three hundred years.

events.title: The Dutch replace the Portuguese and codify the law
events.evidence: The VOC records, and the Roman-Dutch law still in force in parts of the island.
events.becomes: Roman-Dutch law, the Thesawalamai and Muslim personal law codified alongside it, and a canal system in the southwest that is still in use.

events.title: The ordination lineage is re-imported from Siam
events.evidence: The Siyam Nikaya's own records, and the Siamese mission's account.
events.note: The island had given Buddhism to Southeast Asia. It got its ordination line back from Thailand twelve centuries later.

events.title: Kandy falls and the whole island is under one authority
events.evidence: The Kandyan Convention, signed by the chiefs, and the 1818 rebellion that followed it.
events.becomes: Plantation agriculture — coffee, then tea — and the Indian Tamil labour brought in to work it, whose citizenship was still being argued about in the twentieth century.

events.title: Coffee blight, and then tea
events.evidence: The planters' records, the Hemileia vastatrix outbreak, and the conversion of the estates.

events.title: The Buddhist revival and the Panadura debates
events.evidence: The published transcripts of the debates, and Anagarika Dharmapala's Maha Bodhi Society records.

events.title: Watgal and the Raichur doab's Neolithic villages
events.evidence: The Watgal excavation sequence, with a ceramic and lithic record spanning the southern Neolithic.

events.title: Mungbean, horsegram and pigeonpea are domesticated in the peninsula
events.evidence: Archaeobotanical assemblages from Sanganakallu, Watgal and Hallur, with directly dated seeds.
events.note: The southern crop package is not a copy of the northern one. It is an independent invention.

events.title: The ashmound tradition ends and settlement moves downslope
events.evidence: The dated end of ash accumulation at the mound sites and the shift to hillslope villages.

events.title: Megalithic burial spreads across the Kannada country
events.evidence: The cist and dolmen fields at Brahmagiri, Maski, Hallur and T. Narsipur, with their iron grave goods.

events.title: Chandravalli: Satavahana and Roman contact inland
events.evidence: The excavated coins — Satavahana, Roman and a Chinese piece — and the habitation levels.

events.title: The Kadamba script diverges and becomes the ancestor of Kannada and Telugu writing
events.evidence: The Halmidi and Talagunda inscriptions, and the letter-form sequence from them onward.

events.title: The Talagunda pillar tells how a Kadamba founder was insulted at Kanchi
events.evidence: The inscription itself, which gives the dynasty's origin story in the founder's grandson's words.

events.title: The Western Gangas at Talakad, and four centuries of Jain patronage
events.evidence: The Ganga copper-plate series and the Jain basadi record across the Mysore country.

events.title: Kavirajamarga names the Kannada country by its rivers
events.evidence: The text, which defines the Kannada land as lying between the Kaveri and the Godavari and says its people are naturally skilled in poetry.
events.note: A literary treatise that draws a linguistic map. The region defines itself in a book before any state does.

events.title: Pampa writes the Adipurana and a Mahabharata with his patron as Arjuna
events.evidence: Both texts, and the Chalukya court record of his patron Arikesari.

events.title: Ranna and Ponna complete the three gems of old Kannada
events.evidence: The Sahasa Bhima Vijaya and the Shanti Purana, with their court colophons.

events.title: The agrahara network makes the Kannada country a teaching landscape
events.evidence: The grant inscriptions specifying the number of scholars, the subjects taught and the stipends paid.
events.note: Grants that name the syllabus. The endowment mechanic is not invented; it is transcribed.

events.title: The Hoysala and Chalukya tank cascades are cut across the Deccan plateau
events.evidence: The surviving tank chains and the inscriptions recording their construction and maintenance committees.

events.title: Harihara and Raghavanka break the Sanskrit metres for Kannada ones
events.evidence: The Girijakalyana and the Harishchandra Kavya, and the shatpadi metre they established.

events.title: Kumaravyasa's Kannada Mahabharata, sung rather than read
events.evidence: The text, and the gamaka recitation tradition that still performs it.

events.title: The Haridasa movement sets devotion to a teachable musical form
events.evidence: The devaranama corpus of Purandara and Kanaka Dasa, and the Udupi matha's records.

events.title: The Keladi and Mysore Wodeyar lines inherit Vijayanagara's administration
events.evidence: The Keladi and Mysore records, and the continuity of the nayankara assignment system.

events.title: Haidar Ali takes Mysore and builds a modern army out of it
events.evidence: The Mysore state records, the French officers' accounts, and the Company's assessments.

events.title: Mysorean iron-cased rockets are used in the field
events.evidence: The surviving examples taken to Woolwich, and the British accounts of Pollilur.
events.note: Iron casings, not paper. The British took specimens home and Congreve's rockets came out of them.

events.title: Mysore is restored to the Wodeyars as a subsidiary state
events.evidence: The partition treaty of Seringapatam and the subsidiary alliance that followed.

events.title: Kannada printing, dictionaries and the modern prose sentence
events.evidence: The Serampore and Basel Mission presses, Kittel's dictionary of 1894, and the newspaper record.

events.title: The movement to unify the Kannada-speaking districts begins
events.evidence: The Karnataka Vidyavardhaka Sangha's records and the district petitions.
events.note: Kannada speakers were split across twenty administrative units. The map the language drew in 850 took eleven hundred years to become a state.

events.title: Ganeshwar: a copper-working culture supplying the Indus cities
events.evidence: The Ganeshwar-Jodhpura assemblage of copper arrowheads, fish-hooks and bangles, and its typological match with Harappan finds.
events.note: Somebody had to mine and smelt the copper the cities used. This is where.

events.title: Balathal's fortified enclosure goes out of use
events.evidence: The end of the Chalcolithic sequence at the site, with a later reoccupation on top.

events.title: A leprosy case at Balathal: the oldest yet identified
events.evidence: The skeleton itself, with lesions diagnostic of lepromatous leprosy, directly dated.

events.title: The Ahar-Banas settlements disperse into the hills
events.evidence: The end of the Gilund and Balathal sequences, and the continuity of Bhil occupation in the same uplands.

events.title: Iron smelting in the Aravallis follows the copper
events.evidence: Slag heaps and furnace remains in the Khetri and Alwar belts, with associated dates.

events.title: Noh and Bairat: the Painted Grey Ware frontier reaches eastern Rajasthan
events.evidence: The excavated sequences at Noh, Jodhpura and Bairat, with PGW below NBPW.

events.title: Sambhar salt enters long-distance trade
events.evidence: The lake's exploitation record, the Arthashastra's salt monopoly provisions, and the later state salt accounts.

events.title: Zinc is distilled at Zawar by downward condensation
events.evidence: The retort furnaces at Zawar, the slag heaps, and the metallurgical analysis of the residues.
events.note: Distilling zinc requires condensing a vapour below its boiling point. Europe managed it in 1738.

events.title: The Chauhans of Sakambhari and Ajmer
events.evidence: The Chauhan inscription series, and the Prithviraja Vijaya.

events.title: The stepwell becomes the desert's public building
events.evidence: Chand Baori at Abhaneri, Rani ki Vav in Gujarat, and hundreds of others, with their donative inscriptions.
events.note: A water tank you walk down into, built as architecture. Many were commissioned by women.

events.title: The Guhilas at Chittor, and a fort that becomes a symbol
events.evidence: The Chittor inscriptions and the fort's building sequence.

events.title: Alauddin takes Chittor
events.evidence: The Sultanate chronicles, Amir Khusrau's eyewitness account, and the fort's own inscriptions.
events.becomes: A siege that entered Rajput memory as the founding trauma, retold for six centuries — and much of what is now remembered about it was written three hundred years later.

events.title: Dingal and Charan bardic poetry becomes the state's memory
events.evidence: The Charan bardic corpus, the khyat chronicles, and the courts that maintained the poets.
events.note: A caste of professional rememberers on a state salary. The knowledge economy with a job description.

events.title: Mewar refuses the Mughal marriage alliance the other houses accept
events.evidence: The Mughal court records of who submitted and when, and the Mewar chronicles.

events.title: The Mewar and Marwar painting workshops
events.evidence: The dated and signed folios, and the workshop records of the Udaipur and Jodhpur courts.

events.title: Marwari merchant houses build a credit network across the subcontinent
events.evidence: The hundi records, the firm ledgers, and the branch correspondence between Rajasthan, Bengal and the Deccan.
events.note: A bill of exchange honoured two thousand kilometres away, on trust and a family name. The trade system's top rung.

events.title: The Rajput states sign subsidiary treaties and stop being sovereign
events.evidence: The treaties themselves and the Rajputana Agency's records.

events.title: James Tod writes the Annals and fixes a version of Rajput history
events.evidence: The Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan, and the bardic sources he used and did not always distinguish from record.

events.title: The Chhappaniya famine
events.evidence: The famine relief records of the Rajputana states and the mortality returns.
events.note: Named for the Vikram Samvat year 1956. Still the reference point for hardship in the region's speech.

events.title: African millets reach Saurashtra and change the dry-farming year
events.evidence: Directly dated sorghum and pearl millet from Rojdi and Babar Kot.
events.note: Crops from Africa, in Gujarat, before 2000 BCE. Somebody carried them across an ocean.

events.title: Rojdi's long sequence closes
events.evidence: The excavated phases at Rojdi, which run from mature Harappan forms to a millet-based village economy.

events.title: Pastoral groups hold the Kutch and Saurashtra grasslands
events.evidence: The faunal record from the late Harappan sites, dominated by cattle and sheep, and the seasonal camp sites.

events.title: Barygaza's pilots take ships in over the bore
events.evidence: The Periplus, which describes local fishermen piloting vessels through the Narmada's tidal bore.
events.note: The tide runs so fast at Bharuch that a ship needs a local to enter. The Periplus says so, and it is still true.

events.title: The Western Satraps rule Gujarat for three centuries and date every coin
events.evidence: The Kshatrapa coin series, which carries a year on almost every issue — the densest dated sequence in ancient India.

events.title: Gujarat becomes the Jain manuscript country
events.evidence: The bhandara collections at Patan, Cambay and Jaisalmer, and their palm-leaf holdings.

events.title: Anhilwara Patan is founded and becomes the region's capital for five centuries
events.evidence: The Chaulukya and Chavda records, and the excavated remains of the city and Rani ki Vav.

events.title: Rani ki Vav is built by a queen for her husband's memory
events.evidence: The stepwell itself, and the Prabandha tradition's attribution to Udayamati.

events.title: The Jain bhandaras are organised as lending libraries with catalogues
events.evidence: The surviving catalogues, borrowing records, and the manuscripts themselves with their custody notes.
events.note: A library with a catalogue and a lending register, in the twelfth century, funded by merchants.

events.title: The prabandha chronicles record Gujarat's own past
events.evidence: The Prabandhachintamani and Prabandhakosha, written by Jain monks about kings and merchants.

events.title: Gujarat is annexed to Delhi and then goes independent
events.evidence: The Sultanate records and the Gujarat sultanate's own coinage from 1407.
events.becomes: An independent Gujarat sultanate, Ahmedabad, and a naval policy that fought the Portuguese at Diu with an Egyptian fleet.

events.title: Cambay is the western ocean's greatest port until its creek silts
events.evidence: The Arab and European accounts, and the geomorphological evidence for the silting that moved the trade to Surat.

events.title: Diu: the Portuguese defeat a combined Gujarati, Egyptian and Calicut fleet
events.evidence: The Portuguese and Egyptian accounts of the action.
events.becomes: Portuguese naval supremacy in the western Indian Ocean, and the cartaz system that followed from it.

events.title: Surat and Bharuch shipyards build for Indian, Mughal and European owners
events.evidence: The shipyard records, the teak supply contracts, and the European purchases of Indian-built hulls.
events.note: The Bombay Dockyard built ships for the Royal Navy. One of them is still afloat.

events.title: The Gaekwads take Baroda and hold it into the twentieth century
events.evidence: The Maratha and Company records, and the Baroda state archive.

events.title: Sayajirao III makes Baroda's schooling compulsory and its libraries public
events.evidence: The Baroda state education acts, the library department records, and the Oriental Series he funded.
events.note: Free compulsory primary education in an Indian state in 1906, and a public library network to go with it.

events.title: Ahmedabad's cotton mills make it the Manchester of the east
events.evidence: The mill company records, the labour returns, and the textile association archive.

events.title: The Kheda satyagraha: a revenue strike in a failed-harvest year
events.evidence: The revenue department records and the satyagraha's own accounts.

events.title: Terraced wet rice in the Angami and Chakhesang hills
events.evidence: The terrace systems themselves and the comparative ethnographic and agronomic record.
events.note: Some of the most elaborate terracing in Asia, built without a state and maintained by village agreement.

events.title: Iron working in the Brahmaputra valley
events.evidence: Iron slag and objects from the valley's early historic levels, and the Kachari smelting tradition.

events.title: Muga and eri silk are reared in the Brahmaputra valley
events.evidence: The Arthashastra's reference to Suvarnakudyaka silk, and the continuous rearing tradition.
events.note: A golden silk reared nowhere else on earth, and it has been made in the same valley for two thousand years.

events.title: The southwestern Silk Road runs from Sichuan through Assam to Bengal
events.evidence: Zhang Qian's report to the Han court of Sichuan goods seen in Bactria, and the Han and later Chinese accounts of the route.

events.title: The Salastambhas and Palas of Kamarupa keep the valley a kingdom
events.evidence: The copper-plate grant series of both lines.

events.title: The Kalika Purana is compiled in the valley
events.evidence: The text, whose ritual geography is specific to Kamakhya and the Brahmaputra.

events.title: Kamakhya becomes a centre of Tantric transmission
events.evidence: The temple's rebuilding record, the Yogini Tantra, and the Tibetan traditions that name the site.

events.title: The Chutiya, Kachari and Koch kingdoms hold the valley's other quarters
events.evidence: The dynastic records, the Dimapur and Koch Behar remains, and the Ahom buranjis' accounts of them.

events.title: The paik system: every household owes labour, and the state has no cash payroll
events.evidence: The buranji descriptions of the got and the khel, and the paik census records.
events.note: An army, a road corps and a public works department, all paid in land instead of money.

events.title: The Koch kingdom and Naranarayana's patronage of Assamese
events.evidence: The Koch records, and the Vaishnava manuscript production under Naranarayana.

events.title: Madhavdev's Namghosa and the sattra manuscript workshops
events.evidence: The sanchipat manuscripts on aloe bark, and the sattra libraries that still hold them.
events.note: They wrote on aloe bark treated to last. Some of those manuscripts are four hundred years old and still legible.

events.title: The Ahom maidams and the Rangpur palace complex
events.evidence: The burial mounds at Charaideo and the surviving brick structures at Sivasagar.

events.title: The Moamoria rebellion breaks the Ahom state from inside
events.evidence: The buranjis' own account, and the Company correspondence about the appeal for help.
events.note: Seventeen Mughal invasions failed. A peasant rebellion succeeded, and then the Burmese walked in.

events.title: The Burmese occupy Assam
events.evidence: The Burmese and Ahom accounts, and the Company's casus belli for the first Anglo-Burmese war.
events.becomes: The Treaty of Yandabo, annexation to British India, and the tea industry that followed within a decade.

events.title: Assam tea is planted and a labour system is built to pick it
events.evidence: The Assam Company records, the indenture contracts, and the labour commission reports.

events.title: Assamese is replaced by Bengali as the official language, and then restored
events.evidence: The government orders of 1836 and 1873, and the Orunodoi newspaper campaign in between.
events.note: A language removed from its own province by administrative order, and argued back by a newspaper.

events.title: Oil is struck at Digboi
events.evidence: The Assam Railways and Trading Company records and the refinery's own history.

events.title: The Inner Line seals the hills off from the plains by regulation
events.evidence: The Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, and the district administration's correspondence about enforcing it.
events.note: A border drawn to protect a revenue interest, which became the legal shape of the northeast.

events.title: Golbai Sasan: Neolithic to iron age in one section
events.evidence: The excavated sequence, with bone tools, rice, and later iron in stratified levels.

events.title: Rice cultivation intensifies across the Mahanadi delta
events.evidence: The archaeobotanical record from Golbai and Gopalpur, and the delta's settlement pattern.

events.title: Rouletted ware links the Kalinga coast to the whole Bay
events.evidence: The distribution of the ware from Arikamedu to Bali, with Odishan coastal sites in the middle of it.

events.title: Manikapatna: a port occupied continuously for two thousand years
events.evidence: The excavated sequence, with rouletted ware, Chinese celadon, Arab glazed ware and Dutch and Chinese coins.
events.note: One trench, and in it the whole history of who was trading with the Bay.

events.title: The Shailodbhavas and Bhauma-Karas hold coastal Odisha
events.evidence: The copper-plate grant series of both lines.

events.title: Six Bhauma-Kara queens rule in their own names
events.evidence: The Bhauma-Kara copper plates, issued in the queens' names with their own regnal years.
events.note: Not regents. Reigning queens, six of them in succession, issuing grants in their own name.

events.title: The sixty-four yogini temples are built, roofless and circular
events.evidence: Hirapur and Ranipur-Jharial, and the iconographic programme of both.

events.title: The Lingaraj temple and the mature Kalinga building canon
events.evidence: The temple itself, and the Bhubaneswar sequence of some five hundred shrines from the seventh century onward.

events.title: Sarala Das writes the Mahabharata in Odia, and is not a brahmin
events.evidence: The text, whose author names himself a sudra and a farmer, and the manuscript tradition.

events.title: The Panchasakha take devotion into Odia and out of Sanskrit
events.evidence: The five poets' works and their manuscript transmission.

events.title: Odisha is annexed to the Mughal empire
events.evidence: The Akbarnama and the Afghan and Gajapati accounts.
events.becomes: The Jagannath temple's administration passes through Afghan, Mughal, Maratha and finally British hands — and every one of them kept it running, because the pilgrim revenue was worth more than the point.

events.title: The Marathas take coastal Odisha and tax the pilgrim road
events.evidence: The Nagpur Bhonsle records and the Jagannath temple's pilgrim tax accounts.

events.title: The Na'anka famine kills a third of coastal Odisha
events.evidence: The Famine Commission report, which found the deaths avoidable, and the export figures for the preceding year.
events.note: Named for the ninth regnal year. A million dead in a province with a surplus the year before.

events.title: Odia is declared not a language, and proved to be one
events.evidence: The 1870 pamphlet claiming Odia was a Bengali dialect, and the linguistic and literary rebuttal that followed.
events.note: It ended in 1936 with the first Indian province created on a linguistic basis.

events.title: The Madala Panji temple chronicle is examined as a historical source
events.evidence: The palm-leaf chronicle kept by the Jagannath temple's record-keepers, and the scholarly editions of it.

events.title: Inamgaon's diversion channel and embankment irrigate a Deccan village
events.evidence: The excavated channel and embankment, the earliest irrigation works known in the peninsula.

events.title: The Jorwe settlements shrink to a few and then to none
events.evidence: The abandonment sequence at Inamgaon and its neighbours, with the shift to pastoralism in the faunal record.

events.title: Pastoral transhumance becomes the Deccan's way of using the dry season
events.evidence: The faunal assemblages, the seasonal camp sites, and the Dhangar transhumance routes still walked.

events.title: The ghat passes are engineered and the ocean trade reaches inland
events.evidence: The rock-cut steps and cisterns on the Naneghat and Thal ghat routes, and the Naneghat inscription's toll list.
events.note: A pass with cut steps, water cisterns and a published toll schedule, in the first century BCE.

events.title: The Naneghat inscription of Naganika: a queen lists her sacrifices and their fees
events.evidence: The inscription itself, which gives the cattle, horses, villages and cash paid for each rite.
events.note: It is a receipt. The most detailed price list surviving from ancient India is a religious one.

events.title: The Vakatakas rule the Deccan and marry into the Guptas
events.evidence: The Vakataka copper-plate series and Prabhavatigupta's grants, issued in her own name as regent.

events.title: Paithan (Pratishthana) on the Godavari, capital and market
events.evidence: The Periplus's Paithana, the Satavahana coin finds, and the excavated habitation levels.

events.title: The Shilaharas hold the Konkan for four centuries
events.evidence: The Shilahara copper-plate series from north and south Konkan.

events.title: The Lilacharitra: the first biography written in Marathi prose
events.evidence: The text, compiled from the recollections of Chakradhar's disciples and dated by internal evidence.

events.title: The Modi script is adopted for Marathi administration
events.evidence: The Modi document series, which runs from the Yadava period through the Peshwa archive into the twentieth century.
events.note: A cursive script designed to be written without lifting the pen. Millions of revenue documents are in it and most have never been read.

events.title: Eknath edits the Jnaneshwari and settles its text
events.evidence: His recension, which is the basis of every later edition, and his own colophon explaining why it was needed.
events.note: Three hundred years after it was written, somebody sat down and fixed the text. That is the corpus mechanic performed by hand.

events.title: The Peshwas run the Maratha confederacy from Pune
events.evidence: The Peshwa Daftar, some four crore documents, still the largest indigenous administrative archive in India.
events.note: The archive alone is the reason the eighteenth century in India can be written from Indian sources.

events.title: Chauth and sardeshmukhi become a subcontinental revenue claim
events.evidence: The Maratha revenue records and the treaties conceding the claim from Bengal to the Carnatic.

events.title: The Deccan riots: cultivators burn the moneylenders' bonds, not the moneylenders
events.evidence: The Deccan Riots Commission report and the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act that followed.
events.note: They wanted the paper. The debt was the thing that owned them.

events.title: The Marathi press and the public festival as political form
events.evidence: The Kesari and Mahratta files, and the Ganapati and Shivaji festival records from 1893.

events.title: The southern Neolithic villages of the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
events.evidence: The excavated ashmound and village sites of the doab, with their cattle-dominated faunal record.

events.title: Megalithic burials spread across Telangana and coastal Andhra
events.evidence: The cairn, cist and urn fields, with iron grave goods and, at some sites, horse bits.

events.title: Iron working at Kadambapur and the Telangana uplands
events.evidence: Furnace remains and slag with associated dates from the upland sites.

events.title: Dhanyakataka becomes a capital and a Buddhist centre
events.evidence: The Amaravati site's earliest levels, the Satavahana coin finds, and the Ashokan-period stupa core.

events.title: The Amaravati sculptors develop a narrative idiom of their own
events.evidence: The marble slabs themselves, whose crowded, spiralling compositions are unlike Bharhut or Sanchi.

events.title: Nagarjunakonda's monasteries are endowed largely by women of the royal house
events.evidence: The site's donative inscriptions, which name the Ikshvaku queens and princesses as the principal donors.
events.note: Read the donor list. It is mostly women, and they are named.

events.title: The Vishnukundins hold the Krishna-Godavari delta
events.evidence: The Vishnukundin copper-plate series and the Undavalli cave temples.

events.title: Telugu inscriptions multiply and the language takes a written form
events.evidence: The Kalamalla, Erragudipadu and later inscription series, and the shift from Prakrit and Sanskrit formulae.

events.title: The Kakatiya tank cascades irrigate an upland with no river
events.evidence: The Pakhal, Ramappa and Laknavaram tanks, and the inscriptions recording their construction and their maintenance committees.
events.note: Thousands of linked tanks on a plateau with no perennial river. Most are still in use.

events.title: Kakatiya inscriptions record donors from outside the old landed families
events.evidence: The inscription corpus, in which nayaka and cultivator donors appear in numbers for the first time.

events.title: The Reddi and Velama kingdoms hold the delta after the Kakatiyas
events.evidence: The Reddi and Velama inscription and literary records.

events.title: Srinatha writes for four courts and describes each of them
events.evidence: His works and their dedications, and the court records that corroborate the patronage.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya writes the Amuktamalyada, and it contains advice on statecraft
events.evidence: The text, whose chapters on how to treat merchants and forest peoples read as policy.
events.note: An emperor's poem that tells you to keep the forest peoples on your side because they know the roads.

events.title: The Golconda mines are the world's only diamond source
events.evidence: Tavernier's account of visiting the mines, and the European trade records.

events.title: Coromandel kalamkari and painted cottons reach Europe and Southeast Asia
events.evidence: The Dutch and English factory orders with their pattern specifications, and the surviving textiles.

events.title: The Nizam's dominions become the largest princely state
events.evidence: The Asaf Jahi records and the subsidiary treaty of 1798.

events.title: The campaign for a modern written Telugu splits the literary establishment
events.evidence: The Gidugu Ramamurthy and Vavilala pamphlet war, and the eventual adoption of the spoken register.

events.title: The movement for a Telugu-speaking province begins
events.evidence: The Andhra Mahasabha proceedings from Bapatla onward.

events.title: Wet rice below sea level in Kuttanad
events.evidence: The bunded field systems and the sediment record of their reclamation.
events.note: Farmland below the level of the water beside it, kept dry by bunds and pumps. It predates the Dutch polders.

events.title: The Muziris papyrus prices a single shipload
events.evidence: The Vienna papyrus, a Greek contract that itemises a cargo of pepper, ivory and nard with its Alexandria customs value.
events.note: One ship, one contract, and a value equal to a large Egyptian estate. The pepper trade was not a trickle.

events.title: Pattanam's wharf, warehouses and imported goods
events.evidence: The excavated wharf and bollards, the amphora sherds, and the Mediterranean and West Asian glass.

events.title: The Mushika kingdom of north Kerala
events.evidence: The Mushikavamsa and the Ezhimala inscriptions.

events.title: The Nambudiri settlements and the sixty-four gramams take institutional shape
events.evidence: The temple grant record and the Keralolpatti tradition, which is late and tendentious and still the only account.

events.title: Matrilineal inheritance becomes the region's dominant property system
events.evidence: The temple and household records of taravad property, and the colonial-era legal commissions that documented it.
events.note: Property and descent through the mother's line, for most of the population, for nine centuries.

events.title: The Jewish copper plates grant a merchant seventy-two privileges
events.evidence: The plates themselves, held at Kochi, granting rights to Joseph Rabban and his descendants.

events.title: The Kerala temple style: timber roofs, circular sanctums, and a monsoon to survive
events.evidence: The surviving temples and their carpentry, and the Tantrasamuchaya's building prescriptions.

events.title: The Kerala school runs for three centuries as a teaching lineage
events.evidence: The succession from Madhava through Parameshvara, Nilakantha, Jyesthadeva and Achyuta, documented in the texts themselves.
events.note: Not a lone genius. A named teaching lineage, teacher to student, for three hundred years.

events.title: Manipravalam and the Lilatilakam's grammar for a mixed language
events.evidence: The Lilatilakam, which sets out the rules for combining Sanskrit and Malayalam and argues for the result as literature.

events.title: Calicut's Zamorin runs an open port and lets the Arab merchants police it
events.evidence: Ma Huan's and Abdur Razzaq's accounts, and the Portuguese descriptions of the arrangements they displaced.

events.title: Ezhuthachan fixes the Malayalam script and the language's literary form
events.evidence: The Adhyatmaramayanam kilippattu and the script reform attributed to him.

events.title: Kathakali takes form out of older temple theatre
events.evidence: The attakatha texts and the Kottarakkara and Kottayam court records.

events.title: Marthanda Varma builds Travancore and dedicates it to a god
events.evidence: The Travancore state records and the Trippadidanam of 1750.

events.title: Travancore and Cochin fund schooling, and literacy climbs early
events.evidence: The royal rescript of 1817 on state-funded education, and the census literacy series that follows.
events.note: A state deciding in 1817 that it would pay to teach everyone. The results are still visible in the numbers.

events.title: The Channar revolt: the right to cover the upper body
events.evidence: The Travancore proclamations of 1829 and 1859 and the missionary and state correspondence.

events.title: Malayalam printing, dictionaries and the first newspapers
events.evidence: The CMS Press at Kottayam, Gundert's dictionary of 1872, and the Rajyasamacharam files.

events.title: Adichanallur's urn field is excavated and re-excavated
events.evidence: The 1876 and 2004 excavations, the iron and bronze grave goods, and the potsherd graffiti.

events.title: Megalithic burial across the Tamil country: cists, urns and hero stones
events.evidence: The burial fields from Kongu to the Pandya country, and the earliest hero stones with them.

events.title: Potsherd graffiti precede Tamil-Brahmi and may be related to it
events.evidence: The graffiti corpus from Sanur, Kodumanal, Porunthal and Keeladi, and the argument about its relationship to the Indus signs.

events.title: The Madurai and Tanjore Nayakas inherit Vijayanagara's south
events.evidence: The Nayaka records, the Mackenzie manuscript collections, and the temple building programmes.

events.title: The gopuram overtakes the vimana and temple towns grow outward
events.evidence: The building sequence at Srirangam, Madurai and Chidambaram, where later gateways exceed the sanctum tower in height.
events.note: The tallest thing stops being over the god and starts being at the edge of town. The temple has become a city.

events.title: The Siddhar poets write medicine, alchemy and abuse of the priesthood
events.evidence: The Siddhar corpus, and the Siddha medical tradition's own textual lineage.

events.title: Arunagirinathar's Tiruppugazh sets Tamil devotion to complex rhythm
events.evidence: The Tiruppugazh corpus and its metrical schemes, still used as a percussion training text.

events.title: The Tanjore Marathas keep a Sanskrit and Tamil library and catalogue it
events.evidence: The Sarasvati Mahal collection and Serfoji II's catalogues.

events.title: Tamil printing begins earlier than any other Indian language
events.evidence: The Thambiran Vanakkam, printed at Quilon in 1578, and the Tranquebar press that followed.
events.note: The first book printed in an Indian script came off a press in India in 1578. Not 1800.

events.title: Caldwell argues the southern languages are a family of their own
events.evidence: The Comparative Grammar of the Dravidian Languages, and the linguistic evidence it assembled.

events.title: The Sangam texts are recovered from palm leaf and printed
events.evidence: U. V. Swaminatha Iyer's own memoir of the search, and the editions themselves.
events.note: He went house to house asking whether anyone had old palm leaf. Most of Sangam literature is in print because one man did that for fifty years.

events.title: The Justice Party and the first reservation order
events.evidence: The party's founding manifesto and the Communal Government Order of 1921.

events.title: Rice and the delta: the eastward shift of the active channels
events.evidence: The delta's sediment and channel record, and the settlement pattern that follows the live rivers east.
events.note: The Ganga's main flow moves east over two millennia and takes the population with it.

events.title: Wari-Bateshwar's fort, roads and Indo-Pacific beads
events.evidence: The excavated mud rampart, the metalled road, the silver punch-marked coins and the glass bead workshop.

events.title: Gangaridai in the Greek and Roman accounts
events.evidence: Megasthenes via Diodorus, Pliny and Ptolemy, all of whom place a powerful delta kingdom with war elephants.

events.title: The Pala illuminated palm-leaf manuscripts
events.evidence: The dated Ashtasahasrika Prajnaparamita manuscripts, many now in Nepal and Tibet.

events.title: Dhaka muslin is woven at thread counts nobody has since matched
events.evidence: The surviving pieces, the Mughal and European purchase records, and the nineteenth-century attempts to reproduce it.
events.note: The cotton it needed went extinct. The technique went with it.

events.title: The mangalkavya: local goddesses, merchant voyages and Bengali verse
events.evidence: The Chandimangal and Manasamangal corpus and its manuscript tradition.

events.title: The Bengal nawabs make the province the empire's richest
events.evidence: The Murshidabad revenue records and the Company's own estimates of Bengal's remittances to Delhi.

events.title: Fort William College commissions Bengali and Hindustani prose
events.evidence: The College's publication list and the munshis and pandits it employed by name.

events.title: Jute becomes Bengal's cash crop and Dundee's raw material
events.evidence: The mill records, the acreage returns, and the price series through both world wars.

events.title: Bose, Ray and Raman: laboratory science in Calcutta
events.evidence: The published papers, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science records, and the 1930 Nobel citation.

events.title: Tamralipta is the eastern coast's great port
events.evidence: The Periplus and Ptolemy, Faxian who sailed from it, and the excavated levels at Tamluk.

events.title: Chandraketugarh at its height: terracotta of astonishing quality
events.evidence: The excavated levels and the terracotta plaques, whose ships, dress and ornament are documentary in themselves.

events.title: Redh: a Kushan-period town with a hoard of three thousand coins
events.evidence: The excavation at Rairh, its iron-working debris, and the punch-marked and Kushan coin hoard.

events.title: The Malava republic strikes its own coins and dates an era by them
events.evidence: The Malava coin series, and the Krita-Malava era used in Rajasthan inscriptions from the first century onward.
events.note: A tribal republic whose calendar outlived it by fifteen centuries. It is still the Vikram Samvat.

events.title: The desert caravan route links Sindh to the Gangetic plain
events.evidence: The distribution of Kushan and Gupta coin finds along the Aravalli corridor, and the later Arab geographers' route lists.
